draft.title: The war begins in Europe
card: Germany invaded Poland on 1 September 1939. Britain and France had promised to support Poland, and they declared war on Germany two days later.
Australia joined Britain at war on 3 September 1939. Prime Minister Robert Menzies announced it, as Australia then followed Britain's lead in foreign affairs.
means lightning war. Germany used fast tanks and aircraft together with infantry to break through enemy lines before they could respond.
Using blitzkrieg, Germany conquered much of Europe by 1940. Its targets included Poland, Denmark, Norway, the Netherlands, Belgium and France.
draft.remember: Poland was invaded in 1939, and fast blitzkrieg attacks then won much of Europe by 1940.

a.q: Why did Britain and France declare war on Germany in September 1939?
opts: Germany had invaded Poland, which they had promised to help
Germany had invaded Britain and its colonies in Asia
Germany had attacked the American naval base at Pearl Harbor
Germany had bombed Australian cities and ports in the north
a.why: Britain and France had promised to support Poland, so the invasion led them to declare war. Pearl Harbor was a Japanese attack in 1941, and Germany had not attacked Britain or Australia by then.
a.clue: Think about who had been invaded on 1 September.

b.q: A student says blitzkrieg was a slow war of long trench battles. What is wrong with this?
opts: It used fast tanks and aircraft to break through quickly
It used only warships to blockade enemy ports
It relied on a long siege of each enemy city
It used only soldiers on foot to move forward
b.why: Blitzkrieg means lightning war, and its speed let Germany conquer much of Europe by 1940. Long trench battles belong to the First World War.

a.best: Germany had invaded Poland, which they had promised to help

b.best: It used fast tanks and aircraft to break through quickly
